chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from Salih ibn Abi Hammad, from a man from the Kufians, from Abu Khalid al-Kabuli, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said:

Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made the Religion two governments: the government of Adam, and it is the government of Allah, and the government of Iblis. So whenever Allah wants to be worshipped publicly, it is the government of Adam, and whenever Allah wants to be worshipped in private, it is the government of Iblis, and the one who publicizes what Allah wants to be a secret is one who departs from the Religion.
ai.seo_question: What is the difference between the government of Adam and the government of Iblis in Shia theology?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) delineates two distinct modes of religious practice: the 'government of Adam,' characterized by public, open worship, and the 'government of Iblis,' associated with private, concealed devotion. The Imam clarifies that while both are forms of worship, the one who publicizes what Allah intended to remain hidden is considered 'mariq' (departing from the fold of religion), a concept deeply rooted in Shia discussions on *zuhur* (manifestation) versus *kitman* (concealment). This distinction highlights the spiritual hierarchy where public declaration is the norm, but excessive or inappropriate publicity of private acts can signify a deviation from true piety.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Muhammad, from Salih Bin Abu Hammad, from a man from the Kufians, from Abu Khalid Al Kublay, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Made the Religion as two nations – a nation of Adam<sup>as</sup>, and it is the Nation of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, and a government of Iblees<sup>la</sup>. So whenever Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Wants to be worshipped publicly, it would be a nation of Adam<sup>as</sup>, and whenever Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Wants to be worshipped in private, it would be a nation of Iblees<sup>la</sup>, and the publiciser of what Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Wants to be a secret is out of the limits and sanctuary of Religion’.
en.sarwar: 11. Ali ibn Muhammad has narrated from Salih ibn abu Hammad from a man of the people of Kufah from abu Khalid al-Kabuli from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following:

“Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, has made religion into two kingdoms; the kingdom of Adam, which is the kingdom of Allah, and the kingdom of Satan. When Allah wants to be worshipped publicly such time is the time of the kingdom of Adam. When Allah wants to be worshipped in hiding and secretly, such time is the time of the kingdom of Satan. The publisher of what Allah wants to remain secret is out of the limits and sanctuary of religion.”
